I'm looking for a 14-vertex graph that's 3-colorable with girth at least 6 and at least 20 edges. The Heawood graph fits perfectly—it has exactly 14 vertices, 21 edges, girth 6, and is bipartite so it's definitely 3-colorable. I'm recalling that it's constructed as the incidence graph of the Fano plane.

Using the LCF notation [5,-5]^7, I can represent it as a 14-cycle with additional chords: vertices 0 through 13 form the base cycle, then I add edges connecting each even vertex i to vertex (i+5) mod 14, and each odd vertex i to vertex (i-5) mod 14. This gives me the 7 chord edges (0-5, 2-7, 4-9, 6-11, 8-13, 1-10, 3-12) plus the 14 cycle edges for a total of 21. The bipartite structure is preserved since the base cycle is bipartite and the chords maintain that property.
